podcast.title: American Gramophone Label Origin
podcast.body: Chip Davis founded American Gramophone in 1974 as an Omaha-based independent label, initially to release his own instrumental music project, Manheim Steamroller, a synthesizer classical fusion venture. The label later also released C. W. McCall's material. "In 1974, Davis founded American Gramophone, an Omaha-based indie label that he launched mostly to release his own instrumental music, a synthesizer classical fusion project that he called Manheim Steam Roller."

podcast.title: Launch Through C.W. McCall's Success
podcast.body: The unexpected chart success of C. W. McCall, which originated from an ad campaign for sliced bread, played a crucial role in launching the musical career of Chip Davis. Davis, who created the music for McCall, ultimately became far better known for his Manheim Steamroller project. "But the most interesting footnote of the CW McCall trendlet was how it helped launch the musical career of Chip Davis, who ultimately became better known for his other project."
